title: Mock 3 · Money Mechanics
blurb: Fees, waterfalls, return multiples, valuation and tax basics.

questions.q: 'Beta' of a stock represents:
options: Its excess return due to manager skill
Its systematic (non-diversifiable) risk relative to the market
questions.explanation: Beta represents systematic or non-diversifiable risk; a beta of 1.0 mirrors market volatility, below 1 is less volatile.
hints: Wrong: that is alpha.
Wrong: unrelated to beta.
Wrong: illiquidity premium is part of alpha in alternatives.
Correct: beta measures responsiveness to overall market volatility.

questions.q: According to the DPIIT definition referred to in the workbook, a start-up must not be older than:
questions.explanation: DPIIT defines a start-up as a business not more than 10 years old and with turnover not exceeding ₹100 crore in any financial year.
hints: Wrong: not the DPIIT criterion.
Correct: not more than 10 years old (and turnover not above ₹100 crore).
Wrong: not the DPIIT criterion.
Wrong: not the DPIIT criterion.

questions.q: The 'hurdle rate' in an AIF is best described as:
options: A guaranteed minimum return promised by the fund
The maximum return the fund can distribute
The management fee as a percentage of commitments
The threshold return investors must receive before the manager earns additional return
questions.explanation: The preferred return or hurdle rate is the threshold return investors must receive prior to the manager receiving additional returns; it is not a guaranteed return.
hints: Wrong: guaranteeing returns is neither permissible nor possible.
Wrong: there is no cap on returns.
Wrong: management fee is separate.
Correct: it benchmarks investor expectations before carry kicks in.

questions.q: In a European waterfall, the investment manager starts receiving carried interest:
options: On each deal as soon as it is exited profitably
Only if the fund is listed
Only after investors receive 100% of invested capital plus the preferred return
questions.explanation: Under the European waterfall, invested capital and then the preferred return are paid in full to investors before the manager gets additional return.
hints: Wrong: that describes the American (deal-by-deal) waterfall.
Wrong: carry is never paid on drawdown.
Wrong: listing is irrelevant.
Correct: capital and preferred return are paid first.

questions.q: Category I and II AIFs may borrow only for temporary/day-to-day requirements for not more than ___ days, on not more than ___ occasions a year, and not exceeding ___ of investable funds.
questions.explanation: Category I and II AIFs cannot borrow except for temporary needs for not more than 30 days, not more than 4 occasions in a year and not more than 10% of investable funds.
hints: Wrong: incorrect figures.
Wrong: incorrect figures.
Correct: 30 days, 4 occasions, 10% of investable funds.
Wrong: 25% is the single-investee limit.

questions.q: Units of a close-ended Category I/II AIF may be listed on a stock exchange:
options: Only after final close, with a minimum tradable lot of ₹1 crore
At any time, with a minimum lot of ₹10 lakh
Before first close to attract investors
questions.explanation: Units of close ended AIFs may be listed subject to a minimum tradable lot of ₹1 crore, only after final close of the fund or scheme.
hints: Correct: listing permitted only after final close; minimum lot ₹1 crore.
Wrong: incorrect timing and lot.
Wrong: listing comes only after final close.
Wrong: listing is permitted subject to conditions.

questions.q: Which of the following is a 'deemed' accredited investor that need not obtain an accreditation certificate?
options: An individual earning ₹1.5 crore a year
A partnership firm with net worth ₹40 crore
A Category I foreign portfolio investor
questions.explanation: Deemed AIs include Central/State Governments, their agencies and funds, QIBs, Category I FPIs, sovereign wealth funds and multilateral agencies.
hints: Wrong: needs ₹2 crore income or other criteria plus certificate.
Wrong: partners must individually qualify and get certified.
Wrong: family trusts follow individual criteria and need a certificate.
Correct: Category I FPIs are deemed accredited investors.

questions.q: In the context of pooling, 'tax neutrality' means:
options: The fund pays no tax under any circumstance
All investors pay the same tax rate
The fund must be set up in a tax haven
The pooled structure should not put the investor in a worse tax position than investing directly
questions.explanation: Pooling should satisfy tax neutrality, i.e. not put an investor in a comparatively adverse position from a tax point of view versus investing individually.
hints: Wrong: business income may still be taxed at fund level.
Wrong: investors are taxed per their own status.
Wrong: not a requirement; complex structures attract GAAR.
Correct: pooling should not create adverse tax outcomes versus direct investment.

questions.q: Which agreement helps protect an offshore investor against repatriation and arbitration risks in India?
options: Bilateral Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (BIPA)
questions.explanation: A BIPA (for e.g. Singapore) helps protect an investor's financial interests in India against hostilities or repatriation risks and covers arbitration.
hints: Correct: BIPA protects investors' financial interests and repatriation.
Wrong: IMA governs manager-fund relationship.
Wrong: SHA is at investee level.
Wrong: governs distribution.

questions.q: A fund has paid-in capital of ₹800 crore, cumulative distributions of ₹200 crore and residual value of ₹1,000 crore. What is its TVPI?
questions.explanation: TVPI = (distributions + residual value) ÷ PIC = 1,200 ÷ 800 = 1.50; equivalently DPI 0.25 + RVPI 1.25.
hints: Wrong: that is RVPI (1000 ÷ 800).
Wrong: that is DPI (200 ÷ 800).
Wrong: arithmetic error.

questions.q: Which metric is also called the 'realisation multiple' because it tells investors how much cash they have actually got back?
questions.explanation: Distributed to Paid-in Capital (DPI) is also called the realisation multiple; it measures the amount paid out to investors.
hints: Wrong: RVPI is the unrealised multiple.
Wrong: PIC shows how invested the fund is.
Correct: DPI = cumulative distributions ÷ PIC.
Wrong: KS-PME compares with the market.

questions.q: If the Kaplan-Schoar PME of an AIF is 0.85, it indicates that the fund:
questions.explanation: If the market-adjusted TVPI (KS-PME) is greater than 1 the AIF outperformed; below 1 it underperformed the market.
hints: Wrong: outperformance needs KS-PME above 1.
Correct: KS-PME below 1 means the market did better.
Wrong: that would be exactly 1.
Wrong: KS-PME is relative, not absolute.

questions.q: Gross IRR of an AIF differs from net IRR because net IRR:
options: Ignores the time value of money
Accounts for management fees, expenses and carry
Includes the manager's salary at investee level
questions.explanation: Gross metrics do not account for management fees, other fees, expenses and additional returns; net metrics include them and are more representative of actual investor returns.
hints: Wrong: both IRRs use time value of money.
Correct: net metrics include the effect of fees and carry.
Wrong: not part of the definition.
Wrong: distributions are central to IRR.

questions.q: 'Affirmative rights' negotiated by an AIF in an investee company are described as:
options: Negative control used only to oppose actions
Positive control: certain actions need the investor's consent regardless of shareholding
The right to receive dividends before others
questions.explanation: Affirmative rights are corporate actions that require the investor's approval irrespective of its shareholding; they are viewed as positive control. Veto is negative control.
hints: Wrong: veto rights are negative control.
Correct: affirmative rights give positive control.
Wrong: exit rights are different (ROFR, tag, drag).
Wrong: that is a dividend/preference right.

questions.q: A down round refers to a financing round in which:
options: The company's valuation is lower than in the previous round
The company raises debt instead of equity
The founders sell all their shares
The company lists on an SME exchange
questions.explanation: A down round is a financing round in which the valuation is less than the previous round, triggering ratchet/anti-dilution protection.
hints: Correct: valuation falls versus the previous round.
Wrong: instrument type does not define a down round.
Wrong: that is an exit event.
Wrong: unrelated.

questions.q: Under the benchmarking framework, for the purpose of reporting and benchmarking, 'Assets under Management (AUM)' of a scheme means:
options: Value of total capital drawn down under the scheme
Market value of listed holdings only
questions.explanation: AUM for benchmarking shall be the value of total capital drawn down under the scheme; reporting is on pre-tax NAV.
hints: Wrong: commitments are not AUM for benchmarking.
Wrong: target corpus is a fundraising goal.
Correct: AUM = capital drawn down.
Wrong: unlisted holdings also count.

questions.q: According to the workbook, setting the hurdle rate too high (say 25%) may:
options: Tempt the manager to take undue risks to earn the incentive
Reduce the manager's carry to zero by law
questions.explanation: If the hurdle looks too ambitious (say 25%), the manager may be tempted to try too hard and take undue risks; it should be fixed reasonably (say 15% in the Indian context).
hints: Wrong: a low hurdle makes the job easier.
Wrong: nothing is guaranteed.
Correct: an over-ambitious hurdle can induce excessive risk-taking.
Wrong: no such legal effect.

questions.q: 'Super carry' refers to:
options: Higher additional return charged by highly sought-after funds with strong track records
Carry paid only to super key persons
A carry taxed at a higher rate
questions.explanation: Super carry or higher carry denotes higher additional returns charged by highly sought-after funds with very strong performance track records.
hints: Correct: high-demand funds negotiate higher-than-norm carry.
Wrong: not related to key persons.
Wrong: carry is earned above the hurdle.
Wrong: not a tax concept.

questions.q: Which section of the SEBI PPM template is described as the longest and forms the basis of the entire investment paradigm?
questions.explanation: Section VII: Principal Terms of the Fund/Scheme is the longest section and discloses in detail the items in Section I and more.
hints: Wrong: glossary is just definitions.
Wrong: lists disciplinary actions only.
Correct: Section VII, Principal Terms, is the longest.
Wrong: an outlook section.

questions.q: The distribution waterfall section of the PPM must illustrate how many scenarios (loss, no profit/loss, below hurdle, equal to hurdle, above hurdle)?
questions.explanation: Section XIII requires tabular scenarios: (a) loss, (b) no profit or loss, (c) profit below hurdle, (d) profit equal to hurdle, (e) profit above hurdle.
hints: Wrong: too few.
Wrong: too few.
Correct: five scenarios are required.
Wrong: too many.

questions.q: Which is generally the MOST preferred exit route for an equity-oriented AIF from a portfolio company?
questions.explanation: Offer for sale through an IPO is considered the most preferred and attractive exit option and has historically yielded the best returns.
hints: Correct: the IPO has historically yielded the best returns.
Wrong: least preferred, worst case.
Wrong: usually a last resort in a going concern.
Wrong: not an exit route.

questions.q: A company has market capitalisation of ₹500 crore, debt of ₹150 crore, cash of ₹30 crore and no preference capital. Its Enterprise Value is:
questions.explanation: EV = equity value + debt net of cash + preference capital = 500 + 120 + 0 = ₹620 crore.
hints: Wrong: added cash instead of deducting it.
Wrong: ignored cash.
Wrong: deducted debt.

questions.q: Which valuation approach is most appropriate for a company in distress that has no future business case?
questions.explanation: Break-up value considers salvage value if the business were shut down; it is used to value a company in distress or without a future business case.
hints: Wrong: suits businesses with high entry barriers.
Correct: break-up value measures salvage value if broken up and sold.
Wrong: no meaningful future cash flows exist.
Wrong: earnings are absent or negative.

questions.q: Business loss incurred at the level of a Category I/II AIF is:
options: Passed through only to non-resident investors
Not passed through; carried forward and set off at the fund level
questions.explanation: Business loss at fund level is not allowed to be passed through to investors but may be carried forward for set-off against subsequent business income.
hints: Wrong: only non-business losses pass through (with 12-month holding).
Wrong: no such distinction.
Wrong: it can be carried forward.
Correct: business loss stays at fund level.

questions.q: The distributor agreement for AIF distribution may be executed as:
options: An agreement between distributor and SEBI
A bipartite agreement (fund and distributor) or a tripartite agreement (fund, investment manager and distributor)
An agreement between distributor and investee company
questions.explanation: The distributor agreement is either bipartite between the fund and distributor or tripartite between fund, investment management company and distributor.
hints: Wrong: SEBI is not a party.
Correct: bipartite or tripartite.
Wrong: investee companies are not parties.
Wrong: it is a formal contract.
